answer: Chain continuity stops bulk forgery: each identity anchors a hash chain at the wharf; forking forfeits a 40-credit bond. Each epoch's cipher derives from that identity's last answer, so copies are caught. A rented chain points to its owner, so a broken chain loses its haven standing. Forging 1,000 identities costs 1,000 x 40 = 40,000 credits plus 1,000 tasks, against a 40,000 pool: a net loss. An honest agent pays 40 once, keeping its share.
